title: A stale install ownership marker can delete a user-owned replacement directory
symptom: Independent review found that --uninstall treats an existing sibling .boxbox-managed marker as permission to remove a directory, even when the directory is a user-owned replacement.

rootCause.summary: The installer trusts marker existence without binding the marker to the current installed object; its existing user-directory test exercised install but not uninstall.

requestedOutcome: Preserve unowned directories and foreign symlinks during install/update/uninstall; remove only positively identified managed installs and avoid partial copies on dependency failure.
decisions: Use matched installation identity rather than marker existence alone.
Add regression evidence before calling installation preservation verified.

actions.description: Implement ownership identity and safe preflight/refresh behavior.
Run stale-marker, foreign-link, missing-dependency and managed-refresh tests; independently review closure.

verification.name: Installer ownership closure
verification.scope: Development install/copy/update/uninstall; public npm installer is a separate surface.
verification.result: 14 focused tests passed; read-only Sonnet closure found no mandatory findings. Source review and executed tests are separate evidence.

related.note: Regression scenarios extend copy isolation coverage.
Full independent finding and related observations.

history.summary: Sonnet found the stale-marker uninstall data-loss path while reviewing READINESS1 alias infrastructure.
Independent R1 review returned BLOCKED; installer preservation was not established for uninstall.
Bound ownership identities, dependency preflight and preservation regressions passed; independent review closed the mandatory finding.
